reason: Saving a project's scope keeps who granted each unchanged grant. PUT /engagements/{id}/scope and the generic scope-policies create/replace/patch routes now share _attribute_scope_grants: a saved grant whose authority (MissionGrant.authority(): risk classes, tool names and targets as sets, plus expiry) matches an unclaimed stored grant keeps the stored granted_by and granted_at (the client's echoed attribution only breaks ties between stored grants of equal authority); new or changed grants are credited to the active operator at save time, and an already-expired new or changed grant is refused. tests/v3/test_api_crud_validation.py holds the three new regression tests (dedicated route unchanged/changed/new/forged, expired refusal, generic replace and patch with the equal-authority tiebreak) beside #581's forgery and smoke-patch tests. tests/v3/test_domain.py covers the MissionGrant model the authority key was added to. tests/v3/test_web_search.py, test_tool_catalog.py and test_tool_suggestions.py save scope fields through the dedicated route whose payload assembly was restructured. tests/v3/test_generic_crud_exposure.py covers the generic CRUD route surface whose ScopePolicy hook changed.
exclusions: Full suites are not approved and are excluded. No UI, native or Playwright change: the UI only echoes grants it read (EngagementPolicySettings and WorkbenchBrowser send scope.grants with expectedRevision) and displays no grant attribution, so frontend, native and playwright are empty. Browser automation's grant coverage check reads only risk classes, targets and expiry, which this change never alters. Python 3.12 only: no version-specific code.
